name: Zostel Spiti, Kaza
summary: The Kaza branch of the Indian hostel chain is where most solo travellers and students land in Spiti. Dorm beds and private rooms, a common area full of road news, and the easiest place in the valley to find people to share a taxi to Key, Langza or Chandratal.
body: Zostel runs hostels across India, and its Spiti property in Kaza is one of the few backpacker hostels in the valley. It offers dormitory beds and private rooms, a common room and a cafe area where travellers plan the next day's loop. For anyone travelling alone on HRTC buses, the main value is people: a notice or a chat over tea usually finds three others to split a taxi for the Key, Kibber, Langza, Hikkim and Komic loop.

Expect hostel standards at 3,650 m. Rooms are simple, nights are cold even in July, and hot water depends on solar heating and the weather. The hostel usually runs in the summer season and may close or scale down in deep winter, so check current status before you travel. Book ahead for July and August, when dorms fill with long-weekend groups from Delhi and Chandigarh.
why: The cheapest reliable bed in Kaza for solo travellers
Easy to find others for shared taxis
Walking distance from the bus stand and market
price_band: ₹600–1,200 for a dorm bed; ₹2,500–4,500 for a private double (indicative)

faqs.q: Is Zostel Spiti open in winter?
faqs.a: It usually operates through the summer season and may close or reduce services in deep winter, when Kaza's water pipes freeze. Check current status before you travel and book directly through Zostel.

faqs.q: Is Zostel Kaza good for solo women?
faqs.a: Yes, many solo women stay here, and female dorms are often available. The hostel is close to the market and bus stand, which makes late arrivals easier.

faqs.q: Can I arrange taxis from Zostel Spiti?
faqs.a: The hostel is the easiest place to find other travellers to share a taxi. Rates follow the Kaza taxi union board, so check the board before you agree a price.

name: Tabo Monastery Guest House
summary: A plain guesthouse run beside the 996 CE monastery complex in Tabo. Simple rooms, some with shared bathrooms, a short walk from the old assembly hall. Sleeping here at about 3,050 m is the gentlest night in Spiti and puts you at the gate for morning prayers.
body: The monastery at Tabo has long offered rooms to visitors next to the complex, and the guest house is the obvious saver choice in the village. Rooms are basic, with simple beds and blankets; some share bathrooms, and hot water may come by bucket on cold mornings. What you pay for is location: the mud walls of the old monastery are a minute away, and the newer monastery where monks hold morning prayers is next door.

Tabo sits at about 3,050 m, lower and warmer than Kaza, so it is the best place on the Kinnaur road to recover after the climb through Nako. Eat at the small cafes along the road, walk to the meditation caves in the late afternoon, and go to bed early. Rooms are limited, so ask ahead in July and August; check current status before you travel.
why: Next to the oldest working monastery in the Himalaya
The lowest, easiest night for acclimatisation in Spiti
Simple, honest prices

faqs.q: Can I book the Tabo Monastery Guest House in advance?
faqs.a: Rooms are limited and booking channels change, so ask through your homestay network or call ahead in season. Outside July and August you can usually find a room on arrival.

faqs.q: Are bathrooms attached at the Tabo Monastery Guest House?
faqs.a: Some rooms share bathrooms and hot water can come by bucket. If you need an attached bathroom, ask when you book or choose a guesthouse in the village.

faqs.q: Are there rules for guests staying at the monastery guest house?
faqs.a: Dress modestly, keep noise down in the evening, do not drink alcohol near the complex and follow the monastery's photography rules inside the halls.

name: Langza homestays
summary: Langza's farming families open their homes to travellers at about 4,420 m, below the Buddha statue and Chau Chau Kang Nilda. Rooms are simple, dinner is home cooked, and the village goes silent after the day cars leave. Sleep here only after two nights in Kaza.
body: Langza has a cluster of family homestays, and staying in one is the best way to see the fossil village without a crowd. Rooms are in the family's flat-roofed house or a newer annexe: thick blankets, a bed or floor mattresses, and attached or shared bathrooms. Dinner and breakfast are usually included, often rice, dal and vegetables, with thukpa or tingmo when the family makes them.

This is the highest night most travellers spend in Spiti, so treat it with respect. Come up after at least two nights in Kaza, walk slowly, drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol. If you get a worsening headache, vomiting or breathlessness at rest, go down to Kaza that evening. Do not collect fossils from the slopes; the village council asks visitors to look and photograph only.
why: A night in a working farming village
Dark skies and quiet after the day cars leave
Money goes straight to local families
price_band: ₹1,300–2,200 per person with dinner and breakfast (indicative)

faqs.q: How do I book a homestay in Langza?
faqs.a: Most families take walk-ins in season, and your Kaza host, hostel or taxi driver can phone ahead. In July and August, ask a day in advance so a room is ready.

faqs.q: Is it safe to sleep in Langza at 4,420 m?
faqs.a: For healthy travellers who have spent two nights in Kaza, usually yes. Do not come straight from Manali. If symptoms worsen, descend to Kaza that evening, and talk to your doctor before the trip.

faqs.q: Is there mobile signal in Langza?
faqs.a: Signal is patchy and depends on the network and the weather. Tell family you may be out of contact for the night.

name: Kibber homestays
summary: Kibber, on a plateau above a deep gorge at about 4,270 m, has a good number of family homestays. In summer they are a quiet alternative to Kaza; in January and February they are the base for snow leopard trips, with one room heated by a bukhari stove.
body: Kibber was the last village on the old trade route to Ladakh over Parang La, and it still feels like a place where travellers rest. Families rent rooms in their stone and mud houses or in newer annexes, with dinner and breakfast included. In summer you can walk to Chicham bridge, watch the village fields being worked and go down to Key Gompa for morning prayers.

In winter Kibber changes role. From January to March, local spotters scan the cliffs for snow leopards following blue sheep, and the homestays heat one room with a stove and serve hot meals to small groups. Water can freeze and bathrooms are basic in that season. At about 4,270 m, Kibber is a night to take after Kaza, not before; check current status before you travel.
why: Base for Key Gompa at dawn and Chicham bridge
The centre of Spiti's winter snow leopard trips
Simple, warm family homes
price_band: ₹1,200–2,000 per person with dinner and breakfast in summer; winter packages more (indicative)

faqs.q: Should I stay in Kibber or Kaza?
faqs.a: Stay in Kaza for the first two nights, then move up to Kibber if you want quiet and an early start at Key. Kibber is about 600 m higher than Kaza, so do not make it your first night in Spiti.

faqs.q: Can I see snow leopards from a Kibber homestay?
faqs.a: Sightings happen around Kibber and Chicham from January to March, but nothing is guaranteed. Go with a local operator and spotters, and expect cold, slow days of watching.

faqs.q: Do Kibber homestays have hot water?
faqs.a: In summer, usually from solar heaters or by bucket. In winter, water often comes by bucket and bathrooms are basic.

name: Mudh homestays, Pin valley
summary: Mudh, at about 3,800 m where the Pin valley road ends, has a cluster of family homestays and small guesthouses. They feed trekkers finishing the Pin–Parvati and Pin–Bhaba routes and travellers who come for ibex at dawn, painted slopes and a night far from the main road.
body: Mudh is the last village on the road into the Pin valley, about 50 km from Kaza, and most of its families now keep a room or two for guests. Rooms are simple, some with attached bathrooms, and hot water comes from solar heaters or buckets. Dinner and breakfast are included, cooked in the family kitchen.

The point of a night here is the morning. Walk out at sunrise with binoculars to scan the slopes for Siberian ibex and blue sheep, or take a village guide. The village is quiet, the river is loud, and the evening light on the banded slopes is worth the drive. Mudh sits a little higher than Kaza, so it is an easy night for anyone already acclimatised to 3,650 m. A local bus from Kaza usually runs in the afternoon; check current status before you travel.
why: End-of-the-road village in a national park
Ibex and blue sheep walks from the door
Meet trekkers finishing the big crossings
price_band: ₹1,200–2,000 per person with dinner and breakfast (indicative)

faqs.q: How do I get to Mudh from Kaza?
faqs.a: A local bus usually leaves Kaza in the afternoon and returns next morning, or hire a taxi for about ₹3,500–5,000 return. The drive is about 50 km and 2 hours. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is there a hotel in Mudh?
faqs.a: No, Mudh has homestays and small guesthouses only. Comfort travellers choose the best homestay rooms; signature trips usually visit on a day trip from Kaza.

faqs.q: Can I hire a guide in Mudh?
faqs.a: Yes, villagers guide day walks and wildlife spotting for about ₹1,500–2,500 per group. For the Pin–Parvati or Pin–Bhaba treks, book a registered agency.

name: HPTDC Hotel Chandrabhaga, Keylong
summary: Himachal Pradesh Tourism's hotel in Keylong is a plain, government-run stay in Lahaul's district headquarters at 3,080 m. Rooms are simple and the location suits a first night above 3,000 m after the Atal Tunnel, with Kardang and Shashur gompas close by.
body: HPTDC, the Himachal Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation, runs hotels across the state, and its Keylong property is the government option in Lahaul. Expect a standard HPTDC hotel: clean, simple rooms, a restaurant serving Indian meals, and staff used to Manali–Leh road travellers. Bookings are made through the official HPTDC website or its offices.

Keylong sits at 3,080 m, about 71 km from Manali through the Atal Tunnel, which makes it a sensible first night above 3,000 m before Jispa, Chandratal or the Leh road. Spend the afternoon walking to Kardang across the Bhaga river or up to Shashur Gompa, eat early and sleep. Some HPTDC hotels close or run reduced services in winter, so check current status before you travel.
why: Government prices in Lahaul's main town
A gentle first night above 3,000 m
Walks to Kardang and Shashur gompas

faqs.q: How do I book HPTDC Hotel Chandrabhaga in Keylong?
faqs.a: Book through the official HPTDC website or an HPTDC office in Shimla or Manali. Confirm the hotel is operating for your dates, as services can change in winter.

faqs.q: Is Keylong a good first stop for acclimatisation?
faqs.a: Yes. At 3,080 m it is only a little above 3,000 m, so most healthy travellers sleep well. It is a better first night than going straight to Chandratal or Kaza from Manali.

faqs.q: Does the hotel serve food?
faqs.a: HPTDC hotels normally have a restaurant with Indian meals, and Keylong's market has dhabas and Tibetan cafes within walking distance.

name: Sakya Abode, Kaza
summary: A long-running family hotel in Kaza near the Sakya Tangyud monastery. Warm rooms with attached bathrooms, a dining room serving Indian and Tibetan food, and a short walk to the market and taxi stand. A reliable comfort base for three or four nights of village loops.
body: Sakya Abode is one of the older established hotels in Kaza and a common choice for comfort trips. Rooms have attached bathrooms with hot water, extra blankets for cold nights and simple, clean furnishings. The dining room serves dal, rice, vegetables, thukpa and breakfast, and the staff are used to travellers arriving tired from the Kunzum or Kinnaur roads.

The location works well. The Sakya Tangyud monastery is a few minutes away for an evening walk, the market and cafes are close, and the taxi union stand is easy to reach for early starts to Key, Langza or Pin valley. Like most of Kaza, the hotel runs mainly in the summer season; check current status before you travel and book early for July and August.
why: Attached bathrooms with hot water
Walking distance to the monastery and market
Long track record with road travellers

faqs.q: Is Sakya Abode open all year?
faqs.a: It runs mainly in the summer season, roughly May to October. Winter operation varies, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Does Sakya Abode have parking?
faqs.a: Kaza hotels generally have space for a car or two near the building; confirm when you book if you are driving your own vehicle.

faqs.q: Is Sakya Abode good for families?
faqs.a: Yes, rooms are warm and the hotel is close to food and the monastery. Families should still plan an easy first day for acclimatisation.

name: Hotel Deyzor, Kaza
summary: A well-known small hotel in Kaza, behind the BSNL office, with warm rooms, attached bathrooms and a restaurant popular with travellers. A good comfort choice for couples and small groups who want to sleep in town and set out on the village loops each morning.
body: Hotel Deyzor has been a familiar name to Spiti travellers for years. Rooms are simple but warm, with attached bathrooms and hot water, and the restaurant serves Indian, Tibetan and travellers' food that suits long drives and cold evenings. The staff can help arrange taxis through the union and share news on the Kunzum and Kinnaur roads.

The hotel sits in Kaza town, a short walk from the market and cafes, so you can rest on your first afternoon and walk out for a light dinner. Kaza is at 3,650 m: even with heated rooms, many guests sleep badly on the first night, so plan an easy day. Book July and August early. The hotel runs mainly in summer; check current status before you travel.
why: Central Kaza location near cafes and the market
Warm rooms with attached bathrooms
Helpful with taxis and road news

faqs.q: Where is Hotel Deyzor in Kaza?
faqs.a: It is in Kaza town, behind the BSNL office, a short walk from the main market and cafes.

faqs.q: Does Hotel Deyzor have Wi-Fi?
faqs.a: Many Kaza hotels offer Wi-Fi, but it depends on the network and is often slow. Plan to be partly offline.

faqs.q: Should I book Hotel Deyzor in advance?
faqs.a: Yes for July, August and long weekends. In June and September you can sometimes find a room on arrival, but booking ahead is safer.

name: Padma Lodge, Jispa
summary: A popular comfort stay on the Bhaga river at Jispa, 22 km beyond Keylong. Wood-finished rooms and riverside tents, a restaurant used to Manali–Leh road trips, and a calm setting at 3,200 m. A good first or last night above 3,000 m on any Lahaul or Chandratal trip.
body: Padma Lodge has served travellers on the Manali–Leh road for years, and it is one of the best-known stays in Jispa. Rooms are wood-finished and warm, with attached bathrooms, and in summer the lodge also offers tents by the river. Meals are taken in the restaurant, where bikers, families and road-trippers swap notes on Baralacha La and the Chandratal road.

Jispa's altitude, about 3,200 m, makes Padma Lodge a sensible place to acclimatise before Chandratal or the higher passes. Walk the riverbank in the morning, visit the small Jispa gompa, and keep the day light. The lodge is seasonal; Lahaul's hotels largely close from about November to April. Check current status before you travel and book early for July and August.
why: Riverside setting at an easy altitude
Rooms and tents for different budgets
Long experience with road travellers

faqs.q: Is Padma Lodge open in winter?
faqs.a: No, like most Lahaul hotels it runs mainly from about May to October. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Padma Lodge good for a night before Chandratal?
faqs.a: Yes. Jispa at 3,200 m is a good place to adjust before the camps at about 4,250 m. Spend one or two nights here first.

faqs.q: Can bikers park safely at Padma Lodge?
faqs.a: The lodge is used to motorcycle groups on the Manali–Leh road. Confirm parking when you book, especially in July and August.

name: Chandratal camps
summary: A group of seasonal Swiss-tent camps in the designated camping area a few kilometres before Chandratal. Beds, heavy blankets, dinner and breakfast are included; some tents have basic attached toilets. This is the only way to stay near the lake, at about 4,250 m.
body: Camping on the shore of Chandratal is not allowed, so local operators set up seasonal camps in a designated area a few kilometres before the lake. Tents have beds and heavy blankets; some have small attached toilets, others share a block. Dinner and breakfast are served in a dining tent, usually dal, rice, vegetables and roti, with tea on demand. Power comes from solar panels or a generator for a few hours.

Nights are cold, often below freezing even in July, so bring a down jacket, a cap and a warm sleeping layer. At about 4,250 m this is a high night: do it after Kaza or after two nights at Jispa or Keylong, never straight from Manali. Camps open once the road is cleared, usually mid-June, and pack up in early October. Check current status before you travel.
why: The only overnight near the lake
A short walk to the lake for dawn light
Dark skies far from any town
price_band: ₹1,500–3,000 per person with dinner and breakfast (indicative)

faqs.q: Can I camp on the shore of Chandratal?
faqs.a: No. Camping is allowed only in the designated area a few kilometres before the lake. Walk the last stretch and leave nothing behind.

faqs.q: How cold is it in the Chandratal camps?
faqs.a: Nights often drop below freezing, even in summer. Camps provide heavy blankets, but bring a down jacket, thermal layers and a warm cap.

faqs.q: Is there mobile network at the Chandratal camps?
faqs.a: No, there is no mobile signal at Chandratal. Tell family you will be out of contact for the night.

name: The Grand Dewachen, Rangrik
summary: The most comfortable hotel in the Spiti valley, at Rangrik village across the river from Kaza. Built in the local style with heated rooms, a restaurant and views of the valley, it is the base for our signature Spiti trips. Comfortable rather than lavish: this is still a remote valley.
body: The Grand Dewachen sits in Rangrik, a farming village about 7 km from Kaza on the far bank of the Spiti river. It was built in the valley's style, with thick walls and flat roofs, and it is the most comfortable place to sleep in Spiti. Rooms are warm, with attached bathrooms and hot water, and the restaurant cooks a mix of Indian, Tibetan and continental dishes.

Staying in Rangrik gives quiet nights and a dark sky away from Kaza's lights, while keeping Key, Kibber, Langza and the Pin valley within an easy morning's drive. The altitude is the same as Kaza, about 3,650 m and slightly above, so the usual rules apply: an easy first day, plenty of water, no alcohol on the first night. The hotel is seasonal; check current status before you travel and book well ahead for July and August.
why: The most comfortable rooms in Spiti
Quiet village setting across the river from Kaza
Easy reach of every village loop
price_band: ₹10,000–18,000 a night for a double with meals (indicative)

faqs.q: How far is The Grand Dewachen from Kaza?
faqs.a: It is in Rangrik village, about 7 km from Kaza across the Spiti river, around 15–20 minutes by car.

faqs.q: Is The Grand Dewachen open all year?
faqs.a: It operates mainly in the summer season. Winter operation is limited or closed, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Does staying in a good hotel prevent altitude sickness?
faqs.a: No. A warm room helps you sleep, but your body still needs time to adjust to about 3,650 m. Rest on the first day, drink water and talk to your doctor before the trip.

name: Hotel Ibex, Jispa
image_query: Jispa village Lahaul Manali Leh road
summary: The most established hotel in Jispa and one of the best in Lahaul, beside the Bhaga river on the Manali–Leh road. Heated rooms, a restaurant and a calm setting at about 3,200 m make it the top of what Lahaul offers: comfortable rather than luxurious.
body: Hotel Ibex has served travellers on the Manali–Leh road for a long time and is the best-known hotel in Jispa. Rooms are warm, with attached bathrooms and hot water, and the restaurant serves Indian and continental food for road-trippers, families and groups on their way to Ladakh or Chandratal. Around it are willows, fields of peas and potatoes, and the Bhaga river.

We use it on signature trips as the last night in Lahaul before the drive back to Manali, or as an acclimatisation stop before Chandratal. At about 3,200 m most travellers sleep well here. Lahaul's hotels are seasonal and largely close from about November to April; check current status before you travel and book early for July and August.
why: Lahaul's most established hotel
Warm rooms beside the Bhaga river
A comfortable altitude for sleeping well

faqs.q: Is Hotel Ibex Jispa a luxury hotel?
faqs.a: It is one of the most comfortable hotels in Lahaul, with warm rooms and a good restaurant, but it is not a luxury resort. Expect solid mountain comfort.

faqs.q: How far is Hotel Ibex from Manali?
faqs.a: Jispa is about 95 km from Manali via the Atal Tunnel and Keylong, roughly 3–4 hours depending on traffic and weather.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Ibex a good stop before Ladakh?
faqs.a: Yes. Jispa's altitude of about 3,200 m makes it a sensible night before the high passes on the Manali–Leh road.
